result: In 73 non-hospitalised adults sampled serially, brain fog (aRR 0.46, 95% CI 0.22-0.95) and muscle pain (aRR 0.28, 0.08-0.94) at 90+ days were associated with failure to clear upper-airway SARS-CoV-2 RNA within 28 days of acute onset.
reason: Measures acute nasal/saliva viral clearance kinetics, not tissue or gut persistence months later; no atlas finding covers early viral clearance (possible new item).

result: In two independent ME/CFS-control cohort pairs (one at rest, one with exercise challenge), markers indicated microbial translocation with a compromised gut epithelium, a suppressed acute-phase innate response and enhanced compensatory antibody responses, linked to glucose/citrate metabolism and IL-10.
reason: Same translocation-marker theme with added exertion and mechanism data; Giloteaux 2016 is cited but this 2023 paper is not; abstract gives no numbers.

result: Reports a suppressed acute-phase innate response to microbial translocation in ME/CFS at rest and after exercise, with compensatory antibody and IL-10 responses.
reason: Measures in vivo plasma translocation and acute-phase markers, not ex vivo whole-blood stimulation responses; already covered by its gut-translocation-lps link.

result: In 106 post-COVID patients followed to 17-20 months, those meeting CCC for ME/CFS stayed severely ill while other PCS patients improved; lower grip strength at onset correlated with persistence.

Compared with 52 matched non-fatigued controls, 37 people with fatigue after mild COVID showed cortical circuit underactivity, autonomic dysregulation and myopathic change in skeletal muscle, with no distinct subgroups on cluster analysis.
reason: Myopathic muscle change matches the LC myopathy/EMG finding; autonomic result is non-specific in the abstract and not clearly orthostatic testing in referred patients.

result: In 37 ME/CFS patients (22 F, 15 M) and 14 controls doing two 6-minute walk tests, female patients had more fatigue after the first walk (p=0.006) but sex differences in recovery were not confirmed and HRV did not change post-exercise.
reason: Low-burden pilot with a different stressor and outcome; does not measure PEM onset or recovery time comparably to the finding.

result: In 1,274 TwinsUK adults, pre-pandemic plasma IL-6 was associated with chronic fatigue in COVID-negative but not in COVID-positive (mild) participants; chronic fatigue was 17% vs 11% (p=0.001) and higher BMI predicted fatigue after COVID.
reason: Tests pre-trigger baseline IL-6 as a predictor of persistent fatigue (as in the IFN-alpha model), not the acute-infection cytokine response.

result: In 2,240 people with ME/CFS or MS completing the DSQ and SF-36, noise and light hypersensitivity were significantly more common in ME/CFS than MS, and people with both hypersensitivities had worse symptoms and function.
reason: Same self-reported sensitivity measure; adds a large sample, a disease comparison and links to health outcomes.

result: In 34 fatigued adults (7 primary mitochondrial myopathy, 22 CFS, 5 other), serum GDF-15 discriminated PMM from CFS (AUC 0.95) and from other non-mitochondrial fatigue (AUC 0.94).
reason: Muscle/mitochondrial differential-diagnosis biomarker not in the index; small sample, no healthy controls; check against newer muscle-exertion-gdf15 if it exists.

result: In 37 Gulf War illness veterans vs 25 control veterans after 30 min cycling at 70% HRR, symptoms worsened sharply (d=1.65) but select structural, adrenergic and immune gene expression fell rather than rose, and gene changes did not mediate PEM.
reason: Same leukocyte gene-expression protocol finds the opposite direction and no mediation, though in GWI rather than ME/CFS.
